title: feat(spec)!: a URL with a special scheme is read for credentials the way a URL parser reads it, however many slashes follow the scheme
body:
Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: narrowed
Skills-docs: none — no value under `skills/**`, the hand-written `content/docs/**`, `examples/**` or `packages/apps/**` spells a special-scheme URL any way but `scheme://` with an `@` in it (repo-wide count at `1f13eb3189`: 0), and the docs state the rule as "a `user:password@` URL is refused", which reads the same after this change; each refusal carries its own prescription.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：连接器实例与数据源驱动配置里的 URL 凭据判定，对特殊 scheme（`http`、`https`、`ws`、`wss`、`ftp`，大小写不限）按 URL 解析器的读法定位权限部分：scheme 之后无论跟几个 `/` 或 `\`（含零个）都整段跳过，再读 userinfo。两扇门共用同一个函数、同一套语法，写入拒绝与读取改写同步变化；其它 scheme 与 `file:` 不变，`scheme://` 写法的读法不变。
- 为什么改：维护者裁决（2026-11-04，第 4 批第 1 项，选 A）：特殊 scheme 的权限部分按 WHATWG 的读法读取，两扇门一个函数一套语法；框架沿用裁决 D（#29875）——检查看到的就是解析器看到的。
- 风险与回滚：破坏性收窄（spec minor，ADR-0087 D3 条目 `url-credential-special-scheme-read-however-many-slashes`）。升级后，特殊 scheme 之后不是恰好 `//`、且按解析器读法带凭据部分的 URL，在校验、构建产物加载与保存时被拒（保存门 422 `INVALID_METADATA`，定位到该字符串，不回显值）。仓内 examples/apps/skills/docs 实测 0 处受影响。已存行不重判；读取隐去凭据部分，原样保存保留库值。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/spec/src/data/driver/url-boundary.ts`（`authorityStart`：特殊 scheme 分支，唯一的语法改动）、`packages/spec/src/integration/connector-entry-url-credentials.test.ts`（新块：逐 scheme × 写法的拒绝、改写与对照）、`.changeset/url-credential-special-scheme-read-however-many-slashes.md`（FROM → TO）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/integration/connector-entry-url-credentials.test.ts src/data/driver/driver-credential-refusal.test.ts src/data/datasource-credential-redaction.test.ts`，预期 3 个文件 1480 个用例全部通过。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

One rule, read the way a URL parser reads it — **a URL with a special scheme is read for credentials the way a URL parser reads it, however many slashes follow the scheme.**

- **Where a special scheme's authority starts.** `urlUserinfoSpan` (`packages/spec/src/data/driver/url-boundary.ts`, internal, never re-exported) is the one userinfo grammar both doors read. For `http`, `https`, `ws`, `wss` and `ftp`, in any letter case, it now starts the authority after the whole run of `/` and `\` that follows the scheme, however long, none included (`authorityStart`). Every other scheme, and a string with no scheme, keeps `scheme://` or a scheme-relative `//`; `file:` carries no userinfo.
- **Both doors move together.** The connector entry (`connectorUrlWithoutUserinfo`: the write's judgement and the read's rewrite) and the datasource doors (`urlUserinfoPassword` / `urlUserinfoUsername` at the write, `redactUrlPassword` at the read) call that one function. No second parser, and no `new URL()` at either door.
- **Where the authority ends is unchanged**: at the first `/`, `?` or `#`. A URL parser also ends a special scheme's authority at `\`; an RFC 3986 parser (the libsql client's, which reads turso URLs) does not, so the longer authority is kept — it holds every userinfo either parser reads.
- The module notes that stated the old start rule (`connector-url-credentials.ts`, `connector-credential-redaction.ts`, `common.zod.ts`, `datasource-credential-redaction.ts`) now state this one.
- ADR-0087 D3 entry `18.url-credential-special-scheme-read-however-many-slashes.ts`, in the family of `18.url-credential-judged-trimmed-and-in-any-connector-string.ts`; changeset `@objectstack/spec` minor, BREAKING, with its FROM → TO (the three-slash spelling included) and the registration marker.
- **Unchanged.** No public export added or removed; no `.describe()` text changed; `file:` and every scheme that is not special read as before; a URL spelled `scheme://` reads as before; a stored row is never re-judged — a save of its served form keeps the stored value, and an edit of the served value stores the edit.

## Tests

Test names state the rule. Every placeholder is fake and every assertion on one is its absence from what a door served.

- `packages/spec/src/integration/connector-entry-url-credentials.test.ts` — new block. For each of `http`, `https`, `ws`, `wss`, `ftp` × seven spellings of the run after the scheme (none, one slash, a backslash, three slashes, a run of slashes and backslashes, an uppercase scheme with none, an uppercase scheme with three slashes): a `user:password@` and a token userinfo are refused at `providerConfig.baseUrl` with a message that never echoes the value; the read rewrites the same URL minus the userinfo; the served form is accepted. The same at a `providerConfig` string that is not the base URL. CONTROL: no userinfo, or an `@` only in the path, accepted and untouched; `file:`, `postgres:`, `libsql:` with no `//` hold no authority; `file:///`, `postgres:///`, `libsql:///` hold an empty one; the `//` forms keep their reading. Refused ⇔ rewritten over every case and control.
- `packages/spec/src/data/driver/driver-credential-refusal.test.ts` — per URL-bearing driver key (postgres, mysql, mongo, turso `url`, turso `syncUrl`): `user:password@host` refused after each special scheme × spelling; CONTROL a bare username and an `@` in the path not refused for a password; no authority without `//` after `file:`, `postgresql:`, `mysql:`, `mongodb:`, `libsql:`; the `//` forms keep their reading. The shared parse (`urlUserinfoPassword`, `urlUserinfoUsername`) reads the special scheme's userinfo, on the cleaned string too.
- `packages/spec/src/data/datasource-credential-redaction.test.ts` — per URL key, turso `syncUrl` included: refused at the write door, served with the password removed and the username kept, the served form passes the write door; refused ⇔ rewritten over the special and the no-authority spellings; CONTROL a string with no authority served as stored.
- **One-shot ablation** (not committed): the special-scheme set emptied through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor 1 → 0, blob `71496e946da8` → `008323104982`), the mutation held only inside the verify lock, with a trap restore. The three files: **406 failed | 1074 passed (1480)** — every failure a refusal, rewrite or parse pin of the new rule, no CONTROL among them; the refused ⇔ rewritten pins stay green under it, as they must (they pin that the two doors agree, which one shared function holds whatever the grammar reads). Restored: blob `71496e946da8` == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty; at HEAD the same three files are 1480/1480.

## Acceptance notes

- **Count of existing values.** Repo-wide `git grep` at `1f13eb3189` (CHANGELOGs included) for a special-scheme string not spelled `scheme://` that holds an `@` before its first `/`, `?` or `#`: **0** hits. The pattern matches each of the spellings above on a control file and excludes `scheme://`, `mailto:` and an `@` in a path.
- **Why the authority's end stays at `/`, `?`, `#`** (What changes, third bullet): reading `\` as the end would accept values the libsql client reads a userinfo from; the longer authority only ever refuses more, never less.
- **The refused ⇔ rewritten pairing** is the one #29875 pinned, extended over the new spellings at both doors; it holds by construction (one function), and the ablation shows the refusal pins, not the pairing pins, are what carry the rule.
- **HTTP save doors**: they parse through `DeclarativeConnectorEntrySchema` and the driver config schemas these tests exercise; #29875's dogfood pins cover that wiring. No dogfood pin added here.
- No other package is touched: `packages/spec` and one changeset.
